settingsPage.title: Settings
settingsPage.subtitle: Application-wide configuration.
settingsPage.appUrlHint: How users reach HomeHub, e.g. https://hub.example.com. Empty: HomeHub answers on whatever address the browser used. Set it to also allow that origin behind a reverse proxy and to pin passkeys to it — an HTTPS address unlocks passkey sign-in and clipboard everywhere. LAN access by IP keeps working either way.
settingsPage.sessionTtlHint: Signed-in sessions roll forward on activity and expire after this long unused.

retention.title: Metric retention
retention.intro: How long collected metrics are kept at each resolution. Older data rolls up, then ages out.
retention.rawHint: Full-resolution samples, 6–720 hours. Powers the 1h and 6h views.
retention.fiveMinHint: 5-minute averages, 1–365 days. Powers the 24h and 7d views.
retention.hourlyHint: Hourly averages, 7–3650 days. Powers the 30d view and beyond.

account.title: Account
account.subtitle: Your sign-in security and sessions.
account.passwordIntro: Changing your password signs out every other session.
account.totpOff: Add an authenticator app so a stolen password isn’t enough to get in.

totpSetup.scan: Scan this QR code with your authenticator app, or enter the secret manually.
totpSetup.enterCode: Then enter the 6-digit code it shows:
totpSetup.recoveryIntro: If you lose your authenticator, one of these codes gets you in. Each works once. Store them somewhere safe — they are shown only now.

disableTotpConfirm.title: Disable two-factor?
disableTotpConfirm.body: Your account falls back to password-only sign-in. Enter your password to confirm.

account.regenerateConfirm: This replaces all existing recovery codes. Enter your password to confirm.
account.passkeysIntro: Sign in with your fingerprint, face, or security key — no password needed.
account.removePasskeyConfirm: Remove passkey “{{name}}”? You can no longer sign in with it.
account.sessionsIntro: Everywhere you’re signed in right now.
account.passkeysInsecureContext: Passkeys need a secure connection — open HomeHub over HTTPS (or on localhost) to add or use them. Existing passkeys stay registered.

form.secretKeep: Leave empty to keep the stored value

pve.hostHint: Hostname or IP, port 8006 assumed — or a full URL like https://pve.lan:8006
pve.tokenIdHint: Create under Datacenter → Permissions → API Tokens, e.g. root@pam!homehub (uncheck privilege separation, or grant the token PVEAuditor + PVEVMAdmin)
pve.tokenSecretHint: Shown once by Proxmox when the token is created
pve.tokenSecretKeep: Leave empty to keep the stored secret
pve.insecureTlsHint: Accept any certificate. Prefer pinning the fingerprint below.
pve.fingerprintHint: SHA-256 fingerprint from the node’s Certificates page, e.g. AA:BB:… — safer than skipping verification

docker.socketPathHint: The Docker socket on the machine HomeHub runs on. In a container, mount it into HomeHub first.
docker.hostHintTcp: Hostname or IP — port 2376 assumed with TLS, 2375 without. Append :port to override.
docker.hostHintSsh: Hostname or IP of the Docker host. HomeHub runs “docker system dial-stdio” over SSH.
docker.tlsHint: Mutual TLS as set up by Docker’s certificate guide. Paste the PEM files below.
docker.secretKeep: Leave empty to keep the stored value

pihole.hostHint: Hostname or IP of the Pi-hole web interface, e.g. pihole.lan or http://192.168.1.5:8080
pihole.passwordHint: A v6 app password (Settings → Web Interface / API → App password), or the v5 API token from Settings → API
pihole.passwordKeep: Leave empty to keep the stored password

adguard.hostHint: Hostname or IP of the AdGuard Home web interface — port 3000 is the default, e.g. 192.168.1.5:3000
adguard.usernameKeep: Leave empty to keep the stored username
adguard.passwordKeep: Leave empty to keep the stored password

dns.insecureTlsHint: Accept any certificate when connecting over HTTPS.

homeassistant.hostHint: Hostname or IP — port 8123 assumed, e.g. homeassistant.lan:8123 or http://192.168.1.10:8123
homeassistant.tokenHint: Create one under your Home Assistant profile → Security → Long-lived access tokens
homeassistant.tokenKeep: Leave empty to keep the stored token

mysql.hostHint: Address and port — 3306 is the default
mysql.usernameHint: A monitoring user with PROCESS and SELECT works best; full features need broader rights
mysql.tlsHint: Encrypt the connection to the server

mongodb.hostHint: Address and port — 27017 is the default
mongodb.usernameHint: Leave empty only if the server allows anonymous access
mongodb.authSourceHint: Where the user is defined — admin by default
mongodb.tlsHint: Encrypt the connection to the server

truenas.hostHint: The TrueNAS web address, e.g. truenas.lan or https://192.168.1.8
truenas.apiKeyHint: Create one in TrueNAS under Credentials → API Keys
truenas.insecureTlsHint: Needed for the self-signed certificate TrueNAS ships with
truenas.usernameHint: The account the API key belongs to. With it, HomeHub uses the modern WebSocket API instead of the deprecated REST API your NAS alerts about.

minecraft.step1: Create the instance — you land on its Setup tab.
minecraft.step2: Download the companion for your server type (Paper/Spigot, Velocity, Fabric, or Forge) and drop it in the server's plugins or mods folder.
minecraft.step3: Pair with the 6-digit code from the Setup tab — either in homehub-companion.properties or with /homehub pair from the server console. The server connects outward; no ports to open.

amp.hostHint: Host and port of the ADS controller, e.g. amp.lan:8080 or https://panel.example.com
amp.usernameHint: A dedicated AMP user is best — HomeHub gets exactly its permissions
amp.insecureTlsHint: Allow a self-signed certificate on the panel.

tailscale.tailnetHint: Your tailnet name from the admin console, e.g. example.com — leave empty for the token's default
tailscale.apiKeyHint: Create one under Settings → Keys in the Tailscale admin console (starts with tskey-api-)
tailscale.autoRenewHint: An info notification each day of the final week; one day before expiry HomeHub mints a clearly-named replacement token, switches to it, and revokes the old one.

caddy.baseUrlHint: Where caddy-reader listens on the Caddy host, e.g. 10.0.0.2:9776
caddy.codeHint: Run `sudo caddy-reader pair` on the Caddy host and type the six digits it prints. The code is single-use and expires in 15 minutes.
caddy.repairNote: To replace the stored token, remove this system and pair it again with a fresh code.
caddy.adminWarning: Do not point this at Caddy's admin API (port 2019) — it has no authentication and must never leave loopback. The helper is the only safe surface.
caddy.installTitle: No helper yet? Install it on the Caddy host:

aperture.baseUrlHint: The origin your browser also reaches, e.g. https://aperture.example.com
aperture.apiKeyHint: Settings → Integrations → API tokens in Aperture, created by an admin with scopes media:live, system:read, storage:read, cameras:read (starts with apt_)

mc.sshHostHint: Optional: the machine running this network, for full restarts.
mc.sshSecretHint: Password or key — one is enough. Stored encrypted, never shown again.
mc.sshKeyHint: PEM/OpenSSH format. Preferred over a password.

systems.title: Systems
systems.subtitle: Everything HomeHub is connected to — add, test, and manage systems here.
systems.deleteConfirmBody: HomeHub forgets this system and its stored credentials. Nothing is changed on the system itself.

actions.stopConfirmBody: This pulls the plug — the guest OS gets no chance to shut down cleanly. Use “Shut down” for a graceful stop.
actions.deleteConfirmBody: The guest and its disks are destroyed permanently. This cannot be undone.
actions.deletePurge: Also remove from backup jobs and HA

guest.cloneFull: Full clone (independent copy of all disks)
guest.snapshotRollbackConfirmBody: The guest’s current disk state is replaced by this snapshot. Everything since is lost.
guest.snapshotDeleteConfirmBody: The restore point is removed. The guest itself is not touched.
guest.backupModeHint: Snapshot backs up live with minimal pause; suspend and stop are more consistent but interrupt the guest.
guest.sshIntro: Stored per guest, encrypted. Only used for this SSH option.
guest.sshSecretKeep: Leave empty to keep the stored secret
guest.sshNotConfigured: No SSH access configured for this guest yet.
guest.consoleLead: The guest’s own console, straight from Proxmox — opens directly, no guest credentials needed.
guest.sshSecondaryHint: Alternative to the console — connects over the network and needs stored credentials.
guest.hwDisksHint: Read-only here — resizing or moving disks is too destructive for a quick edit.
guest.hwOtherHint: Advanced — raw Proxmox values, exactly as the API stores them.
guest.hwConfirmBody: Every changed key below is written to the guest’s Proxmox config in a single operation.

backups.scheduleHint: Proxmox calendar event, e.g. 02:30 (daily) or sat 03:00

empty.title: No backup schedules
empty.body: Create a schedule so backups happen without you thinking about them.

empty.title: No containers
empty.body: No containers are visible to you on this host.

actions.bulkStopConfirmBody: The selected containers are sent a stop signal and go offline until started again.
actions.killConfirmBody: SIGKILL — the process is terminated instantly, with no chance to shut down cleanly. Use Stop for a graceful shutdown.
actions.removeConfirmBody: The container and its writable layer are deleted from this host. Named volumes are kept unless you say otherwise below.
actions.removeForceHint: Kills the container first if it is still running
actions.recreateBody: The container is stopped, removed, and created again with its current configuration. Data in named volumes survives; the writable layer does not.
actions.queuedBody: Running in the background — the result lands in your notifications.

container.envIntro: Values stay hidden until you reveal them — this is where secrets tend to live.
container.logsIntro: Streams the container’s output live, starting with the most recent lines.
container.logsTailHint: How many past lines to load before following live output
container.shellIntro: Opens an interactive terminal inside the running container.
container.shellCommandHint: Defaults to bash, falling back to sh

stacks.redeployBody: Every service in this project is recreated from its current compose configuration. Expect brief downtime while containers restart.

empty.title: No compose stacks
empty.body: Containers started via docker compose show up here, grouped by project.

images.pullReferenceHint: e.g. nginx:latest or ghcr.io/owner/app:1.2 — pulled in the background
images.pruneConfirmBody: All dangling images on this host are deleted to reclaim space. Images used by any container are kept.
images.deleteConfirmBody: The image is removed from this host. Containers already running keep working; using it again means pulling it again.
images.deleteForceHint: Removes it even when tagged in multiple repositories or used by stopped containers

registries.secretHint: Sent only to this registry, never shown again
registries.removeConfirmBody: Pulls from this registry become anonymous — private images will stop pulling and updating.
registries.empty: No registry credentials stored. Public images pull anonymously.

danger.dropConfirmBodyCollection: The collection {{database}}.{{object}} and all ≈ {{formatted}} documents in it are destroyed permanently. There is no undo.

setup.sshNotConfigured: Not configured — edit the system on the Systems page and fill in the SSH fields.

typeDescriptions.nfs: An NFS export on your network
typeDescriptions.s3: MinIO, Garage, AWS S3, or any S3-compatible store

targets.runQueuedBody: The result lands in your notifications when it finishes.
targets.secretKeep: Leave empty to keep the stored value
targets.retentionHint: Archives older than this are pruned after each successful backup.
targets.encryptHint: Archives are sealed with this installation’s backup key. Export it from the Encryption key section on this page and store it offline — without it, encrypted archives can’t be restored anywhere else.
targets.enabledHint: Disabled targets are skipped by schedules and can’t be backed up to.
targets.deleteConfirmBody: HomeHub forgets this target and its stored credentials. Archives already stored on the target are NOT deleted.

fields.prefixHint: Optional key prefix to keep archives under

archives.restoreWarningReplace: Restoring replaces the entire current database with this archive’s contents.
archives.restoreWarningLost: Everything created or changed since {{date}} — users, settings, history, everything — is lost.
archives.restoreWarningRestart: HomeHub restarts to finish the restore, and everyone (including you) is signed out.

key.warning: Store this key somewhere safe and offline — a password manager or a printed copy. Anyone holding it can read your encrypted backups; without it, they are unrecoverable.

devices.emptyBody: Devices appear here as they join the tailnet.

devices.exitNodeHint: Allow devices to route all their internet traffic through this machine.

keys.emptyBody: Auth keys let servers and containers join the tailnet without interactive login.
keys.revokeBody: “{{name}}” stops working immediately. Devices already joined stay connected.
keys.expiryHint: 1–365 days. The key stops minting devices after this.
keys.reusableHint: Can register more than one device.
keys.ephemeralHint: Devices vanish from the tailnet shortly after they disconnect — for containers and CI.
keys.preauthorizedHint: Devices skip manual approval when device approval is on.
keys.createdBody: Copy the key now — this is the only time it is shown.
keys.autoRenewBody: Info notification each day of the final week; one day before expiry HomeHub mints a clearly-named replacement, switches to it, and revokes the old token.

dns.magicDnsHint: Devices get names like nas.tailnet.ts.net. Needs at least one nameserver.

caddy.subtitle: Caddy reverse proxy
caddy.degradedBanner: The helper is up but cannot reach Caddy: {{message}}

sites.emptyBody: Add a site and Caddy starts serving it — the change is validated by Caddy itself before anything touches disk.
sites.readOnlyBanner: This helper is read-only, so sites can be listed but not changed. To allow edits, restart caddy-reader on the Caddy host with --writable.
sites.removeBody: Caddy stops serving {{domain}} the moment the change is applied.
sites.advancedBody: Site blocks the editor doesn't model. They are preserved exactly as written — shown here so the list never lies about what the file contains.
sites.globalBody: Applies to every site this Caddy serves.

reasons.tlsAdvanced: tls block does more than a DNS challenge

editor.domainHint: Just the domain — no scheme, no path
editor.extraDomainsHint: Comma-separated, served by the same block
editor.schemeHint: Usually empty; https for a TLS upstream
editor.dnsArgsHint: Kept exactly as written — usually an {env.*} placeholder, never expanded
editor.encodeHint: Arguments to `encode`, e.g. gzip zstd — empty for none
editor.insecureHint: For https upstreams with self-signed certificates.
editor.unknownKept: This block carries directives the editor doesn't model. They are kept exactly as written when you save:

served.emptyBody: The running config has no host-matched routes.
served.proxiedBody: What the running config actually routes, read live from Caddy through the helper.
served.unresolvableBody: These domains are proxied, but where they go can't be answered statically.
served.noProxyBody: Domains answered by something other than a reverse proxy — a file server, a redirect.

setup.title: caddy-reader helper
setup.installStep: Install the helper on the Caddy host
setup.setupNote: It asks a few questions with sensible defaults and ends with a six-digit pairing code. Re-running it later prints a fresh code.
setup.repairHint: Enter the code from the setup command to replace the stored token — after reinstalling the helper, or if pairing was lost.

grid.emptyBody: Aperture reports no cameras this account may view.

assistant.title: Assistant
assistant.subtitle: Answers from your systems' live data · {{provider}} · {{model}}
assistant.offBody: An administrator can enable it in the assistant settings.
assistant.offBodyAdmin: Connect an AI provider and the assistant answers questions about your systems from live data — scoped to each user's own permissions.
assistant.enableHint: Turns the assistant on for everyone. Each user only ever sees what their own permissions allow.
assistant.providerHint: Cloud APIs or a model running on your own hardware — anything OpenAI-compatible works.
assistant.modelHint: The model name your provider expects.
assistant.apiKeyHint: Stored encrypted in the vault, never shown again.
assistant.apiKeySetHint: A key is stored. Enter a new one to replace it, or leave empty to keep it.
assistant.scopeNote: The assistant currently has read-only tools: systems, alerts, metrics, notifications and (with permission) the audit log. It cannot change anything.
assistant.clearBody: Deletes your chat history with the assistant. The assistant keeps no other memory.
assistant.emptyExamples: “Is everything healthy?” · “How full is the NAS?” · “What alerts fired today?”
assistant.baseUrlHint: Where the API lives. Prefilled with the runtime's usual address — change it if yours runs elsewhere.
assistant.apiKeyOptionalHint: Local runtimes usually need no key — leave empty unless yours requires one.
assistant.scanEmpty: No LM Studio found. Make sure its server is running and “Serve on Local Network” is enabled.
assistant.endpointOkEmpty: Reachable, but no model is loaded yet.
assistant.lmGuide1: In LM Studio, open the Developer tab and start the server.
assistant.lmGuide2: Enable “Serve on Local Network” — otherwise it only listens on that machine.
assistant.lmGuide3: Load a model (one that supports tool use answers questions best).
assistant.lmGuide4: The endpoint is http://<that machine's IP>:1234/v1 — find it above or test it here.
assistant.apiKeyStoredHint: A key for {{provider}} is stored — each provider keeps its own. Enter a new one to replace it, or leave empty to keep it.
assistant.scanLocked: found — requires its API key (enter it below, then test)

telegram.title: Telegram bridge
telegram.subtitle: Talk to the assistant from Telegram — it answers there and can act on your homelab.
telegram.step1b: on Telegram, send /newbot, and copy the token it gives you.
telegram.step2: Paste the token below, enable the bridge, and save.
telegram.step3: In your chat with the bot, send /link — it replies with a code.
telegram.tokenStored: A token is stored — paste a new one only to replace it.
telegram.noChats: No chats linked yet — plain messages from a linked chat go straight to the assistant.
telegram.modes: Plain messages talk to the AI assistant under the linked user's permissions. Messages starting with ! or / are command triggers — configurable soon.
telegram.step4: Type that code here (below) while signed in. Nothing links until you do.
telegram.enterCode: Send /link to {{bot}}, then enter the code it gives you here:
